items.title: Lesson Podcast
items.description: Audio guide to social loafing, deindividuation, and how crowd membership affects prosocial and antisocial behaviour.

items.title: Social Influence — Psychology Lecture Series
items.description: Lecture episode covering group processes including deindividuation and social loafing — closely matched to the AQA crowd behaviour content.

items.title: Crowd Psychology: Deindividuation, Groupthink, and Inaction
items.description: Explores the forces that govern crowd behaviour, including deindividuation and why groups can suppress individual morality.

items.title: Social Facilitation, Social Loafing, and Deindividuation
items.description: Lecture covering all three group-behaviour concepts in one clear session — ideal for covering the whole lesson topic quickly.

items.title: Deindividuation: The Real Cause of Mob Behaviour
items.description: Explains why individuals in crowds lose self-awareness and act in ways they normally would not, with real-world examples.

items.title: Die Welle / The Wave (2008)
items.description: Classroom experiment turns a German school group into a fascist-like collective — a powerful illustration of deindividuation and group conformity.

items.title: Crowd Behavior and Deindividuation (Intro Psych Tutorial #202)
items.description: Concise tutorial explaining how crowds can trigger behaviours that individuals would never engage in alone.

items.title: BBC Bitesize — AQA GCSE Psychology
items.description: Bitesize revision hub with notes and quizzes on crowd behaviour, deindividuation, and social loafing for AQA GCSE.

items.title: AQA GCSE Psychology specification
items.description: Official AQA spec page — check exactly which aspects of collective behaviour are assessed in the exam.
